newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian markets outpaced in region - survey.
newsitem.headline: Australian markets outpaced in region - survey.

text.p: Australia's foreign exchange market has lost significant ground to other major centres within the region since 1989, a survey conducted by the Securities Industry Research Centre of Asia-Pacific (SIRCA) showed.
The Australia Stock Exchange (ASX) has also been outpaced within the region, and only the market for interest rate derivatives exhibits a far more regionally competitive position.

"The evidence suggested that the relatively greater and improving liquidity in other financial centres would result in a continuing trend of regionalisation to our counterparts away from Australia," SIRCA said.
"This would result in further losses of liquidity in Australian markets and thus reduce or redirect savings and investment to overseas markets," the report said.

SIRCA said this evidence was supported by interviews with over 35 percent of active over-the-counter participants, and of concern was a lack of concentrated government and industry action to reverse this trend.

The survey, which was commissioned by the Australian Financial Markets Association (AFMA), showed that forex has grown in this period, but the market has a strong bias towards local currency transactions with volumes of 34.3 percent.
The foreign exchange market of Singapore and Hong Kong display significantly higher levels of activity and can be expected to attract further participants into these markets.

Although ranked ninth in the world in terms of foreign exchange turnover, Australia's world market share was only 3.0 percent compared with Singapore (ranked 4th) with a 7.0 percent share and Hong Kong (5th) with 6.0 percent.
The ASX has also been steadily positive, but again the survey demonstrated that it was not keeping pace with its regional counterparts.
Despite a record turnover of A$133 billion in 1995, Australia is ranked only fourth in the Asia-Pacific behind Taiwan, Korea and Hong Kong, which had a turnover of A$143 billion.
However, Australia's interest rate derivatives market exhibits a far more regionally competitive position than foreign exchange, SIRCA said.

The share of business undertaken with end users in Australia dwarfs that of Hong Kong and Singapore and after adjusting for the volume of Euro-yen transactions undertaken in Singapore, the volumes traded are evenly spread with Australia accounting for about one-third of the regions volumes.

But a downturn in the level of domestic activity is likely to lead to substantially reduced market volumes and present a threat that participants in these markets will also gravitate towards Hong Kong and Singapore, SIRCA added.
